_**Agent (copilot/claude-sonnet-5)**_

**Cause:** The named volume `retaildw-data` (mounted at `/var/opt/mssql`) already exists from a previous run — likely created before the `mssql.conf` bind mount was added to `docker-compose.yml#L20`. At that time, Docker auto-created `/var/opt/mssql/mssql.conf` as a **directory** placeholder inside the volume. Now the compose file tries to bind-mount the host file `mssql.conf` (a regular file) onto that same path, and Docker refuses because file→directory (or vice versa) mounts aren't allowed:

```
mount src=...mssql.conf, dst=/var/opt/mssql/mssql.conf: not a directory
```

Confirmed: `infoshare-silkycoders-sql-ai-1_retaildw-data` volume already exists.

**Fix options:**
1. Remove the stale volume so SQL Server initializes fresh and the bind mount succeeds — but this **deletes any data** in that volume (any DB state from prior workshop runs).
2. Alternatively, exec into the volume via a throwaway container and delete just the `/var/opt/mssql/mssql.conf` directory, preserving other data.

Since this is destructive, do you want me to run `docker compose down -v` (removes the volume) or take the more surgical approach (option 2) to preserve existing data?

wsl_memory() { # cmd_wsl_memory [GB] - ensure .wslconfig grants WSL2 enough RAM for sqlservr (>=2000MB required)
  local target_gb="${1:-$WSL_MIN_MEMORY_GB}"
  local target="${target_gb}GB"
  local winhome="${USERPROFILE:-}"
  if [ -z "$winhome" ]; then
    echo "USERPROFILE is not set - cannot locate .wslconfig" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  local cfg
  if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    cfg="$(cygpath -u "$winhome")/.wslconfig"
  else
    cfg="$winhome/.wslconfig"
  fi

  if [ -f "$cfg" ] && grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*memory[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*${target}[[:space:]]*\$" "$cfg"; then
    echo "WSL2 memory already set to $target in $cfg - no change"
    return 0
  fi

  touch "$cfg"
  if ! grep -q '^\[wsl2\]' "$cfg"; then
    printf '[wsl2]\n%s\n' "$(cat "$cfg")" > "$cfg.tmp" && mv "$cfg.tmp" "$cfg"
  fi
  if grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*memory[[:space:]]*=' "$cfg"; then
    sed -i -E "s/^[[:space:]]*memory[[:space:]]*=.*/memory=${target}/" "$cfg"
  else
    awk -v line="memory=${target}" '{ print } /^\[wsl2\]/ && !done { print line; done=1 }' "$cfg" > "$cfg.tmp" && mv "$cfg.tmp" "$cfg"
  fi

  echo "updated $cfg -> memory=${target}"
  echo "restarting WSL to apply new memory limit..."
  wsl.exe --shutdown
  echo "WSL restarted. Start Docker Desktop again before running './scripts/dw.sh up'."
}

cmd_
